mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals a broad collapse in out-of-home activity that suppresses impulse shopping and discretionary visits, so RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks than in the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remaining deeply negative.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises above 35 points, households substitute away from trips to shops and restaurants because time spent at home dominates daily activity, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within one week and into the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 35 points, or instead rises while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates non-retail local trips are absorbing errand demand and leisure time, which diverts traffic from shopping venues and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next two to four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall over the next 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are both rising together.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls by more than 15 points week-on-week, access friction to commercial areas rises immediately and retail visits drop in the following week, making RETAIL_REC lower over the next seven days.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not weaken within one week after a weekly TRANSIT drop greater than 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling WORKPLACES and falling TRANSIT identifies a worsening commuting shock that removes both weekday foot traffic and trip chaining, producing further deterioration in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 28 days even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to fall together.

mechanism_narrative: A fast rise in PARKS followed by weaker retail visits marks a shift toward local outdoor leisure over shopping, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks after PARKS accelerates upward.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points in a single week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after PARKS jumps upward by at least 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a sustained easing in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals that commuting returns are stalled rather than expanding, so retail demand remains suppressed and RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: During reopening, RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed or keep falling.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM turns negative while RESIDENTIAL keeps rising, the pattern indicates households are consolidating trips at home and avoiding discretionary shopping, which pushes RETAIL_REC lower within two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 20 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM is negative and RESIDENTIAL remains above 20 points.
